input: const order = await ordersCollection.find({ email: updatedEmail })

context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Stop trusting the email from the request. Require authentication on every method of this route (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, etc.), and take the caller's identity from the verified session or token (for example req.user.id or req.user.email), not from the path or body. Scope the query to that principal, for example find({ userId: req.user.id }), so the caller can only read orders they own. If the route must serve other principals, allow it only when a server-side role check (such as admin) passes, and return 401 for unauthenticated requests and 403 or 404 for ownership mismatches. Prefer an immutable user ID over email for ownership, since email can change, and avoid querying by an email supplied in the request. Apply the same ownership check to every method on the route, and log access to Personal Data.
